meaning: Master of Philosophy
plain_explanation: The research degree this thesis is written for.

meaning: University of Mines and Technology, Tarkwa
plain_explanation: The university where the thesis is submitted.

meaning: Dissolved Gas Analysis
plain_explanation: Measuring the gases dissolved in transformer oil to find faults inside the transformer without opening it.

meaning: parts per million
plain_explanation: Amount of gas in the oil; 1 ppm = 1 microlitre of gas in 1 litre of oil.

meaning: hydrogen
plain_explanation: Gas formed mainly by partial discharges (low-energy electrical activity) in the oil.

meaning: methane
plain_explanation: Hydrocarbon gas formed when oil is overheated, mainly at the lower fault temperatures.

meaning: ethane
plain_explanation: Hydrocarbon gas formed when oil is overheated, mainly at the lower fault temperatures.

meaning: ethylene
plain_explanation: Hydrocarbon gas favoured above about 500 °C; it rises as thermal faults get hotter.

meaning: acetylene
plain_explanation: Gas that needs at least 800 to 1 200 °C; formed in significant amounts mainly in electrical arcs.

meaning: carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide
plain_explanation: Gases formed mainly when paper insulation breaks down; not used in this thesis (decision D2).

meaning: no fault
plain_explanation: A transformer without a fault: its gases stay at the levels normally found in service.

meaning: partial discharges
plain_explanation: Small electrical discharges that only partly bridge the insulation (corona type, can form X-wax, or small sparking punctures in paper).

meaning: discharges of low energy
plain_explanation: Sparking or tracking: larger punctures in paper, carbonised paper surface or carbon particles in oil.

meaning: discharges of high energy
plain_explanation: Arcing with power follow-through: extensive carbonisation, metal fusion, sometimes tripping of the equipment.

meaning: thermal fault below 300 °C
plain_explanation: Overheating in which the paper has turned brownish.

meaning: thermal fault 300 to 700 °C
plain_explanation: Overheating in which the paper has carbonised.

meaning: thermal fault above 700 °C
plain_explanation: Very hot fault: carbonised oil, metal colouring (800 °C) or metal fusion (above 1 000 °C).

meaning: T1 or T2 (merged class)
plain_explanation: Used in this project when a source does not say whether the thermal fault was below or above 300 °C.

meaning: mixture of thermal and electrical faults
plain_explanation: A zone of the Duval Triangle 1 for cases that look partly thermal and partly electrical.

meaning: non-significant
plain_explanation: In the IEC ratio table: this ratio is not used for that fault, whatever its value.

meaning: on-load tap changer
plain_explanation: A switch that changes the transformer's voltage ratio while it is in service; its sparking makes gases that can leak into the main tank.

term: P, U, R, I, B, C, S
meaning: equipment codes of the IEC TC 10 database
plain_explanation: P power transformer without, U with a communicating OLTC; R reactor; I instrument transformer; B bushing; C cable; S tap-changer selector compartment.

meaning: low voltage, high voltage
plain_explanation: The lower- and higher-voltage sides (windings, connections) of a transformer.

meaning: International Electrotechnical Commission
plain_explanation: The world body that publishes electrical standards, such as IEC 60599.

meaning: IEC guide to the interpretation of dissolved and free gas analysis
plain_explanation: The international standard that defines the fault types and the IEC gas-ratio method.

meaning: IEC Technical Committee 10 (fluids for electrotechnical applications)
plain_explanation: The committee that wrote IEC 60599; its database of 117 inspected faulty units is this thesis's main benchmark.

meaning: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers
plain_explanation: A professional body that publishes engineering standards and journals.

meaning: IEEE guide for the interpretation of gases generated in oil-immersed transformers
plain_explanation: The IEEE standard that contains the Duval Triangle 1 (2019 edition) and the Rogers ratio table (2008 edition).

meaning: iTeh Standards
plain_explanation: A standards distributor that publishes official free previews of standards.

meaning: Creative Commons Attribution licence
plain_explanation: An open-access licence: the paper may be read and reused freely if the authors are credited.

meaning: diagnosis from gas ratios
plain_explanation: Divides one gas by another (for example C2H2/C2H4) and compares the result with fixed limits to name the fault.

meaning: graphical DGA method by M. Duval
plain_explanation: The shares of CH4, C2H4 and C2H2 are plotted as one point in a triangle divided into fault zones.

meaning: older gas-ratio method by R.R. Rogers
plain_explanation: A ratio table that names faults from three gas ratios; kept in IEEE C57.104.

meaning: 90 % typical gas concentrations
plain_explanation: Levels below which about 90 % of transformers in service are found; not limit values.

meaning: rule that lets conventional methods answer 'Normal'
plain_explanation: If all gases are below their typical values, the conventional methods give Normal instead of a fault (decision D3).

meaning: machine learning
plain_explanation: Computer methods that learn the link between gas values and fault type from labelled examples.

meaning: support vector machine
plain_explanation: A classifier that separates classes with the widest possible boundary.

meaning: random forest
plain_explanation: Many decision trees, each trained on a random sample; they vote for the answer.

meaning: extreme gradient boosting
plain_explanation: Decision trees built one after another, each correcting the errors of the previous ones.

meaning: multilayer perceptron
plain_explanation: A small artificial neural network with layers of connected units.

meaning: multinomial logistic regression
plain_explanation: A simple, explainable model that turns weighted gas values into class probabilities.

meaning: SHapley Additive exPlanations
plain_explanation: Shows how much each gas pushed a model's decision towards or away from each fault.

meaning: fixed reference test set
plain_explanation: The IEC TC 10 cases whose faults were confirmed by inspection; every method is scored on them.

meaning: fault confirmed by opening the equipment
plain_explanation: The fault type was seen by engineers after the unit was opened, not guessed from the gases.

meaning: records used to build the models
plain_explanation: 439 clean records from the Dissanayake training file.

meaning: Dissanayake unseen test file
plain_explanation: 70 records (61 independent of the benchmark) kept away from training.

meaning: Li (2019) dataset
plain_explanation: 201 records from a different source (86 independent of the benchmark), used to test the models on new data.

meaning: stand-in value
plain_explanation: A fake tiny number written where no measurement was available; treated as not detected (D8).

meaning: gas below the laboratory's detection limit
plain_explanation: Treated as 0 ppm in this thesis (decision D8).

meaning: test cases hidden in the training data
plain_explanation: If a model has already seen a test case, its score is falsely high.

meaning: main analysis and its repeat under another reasonable choice
plain_explanation: The sensitivity analysis shows whether the conclusion changes when a choice is made differently.

meaning: records with all five gases reported
plain_explanation: Used only for the sensitivity analysis.

meaning: provenance record of a dataset
plain_explanation: States where a dataset came from, its licence, its fingerprint and known problems.

meaning: translation table of fault labels
plain_explanation: Lists every original label, its new code and the reason.

meaning: Secure Hash Algorithm, 256-bit
plain_explanation: A file's digital fingerprint: if one byte of the file changes, the fingerprint changes.

meaning: repeated train-and-test on parts of the training data
plain_explanation: The data are split into parts; each part is used once for testing while the others train the model.

meaning: one part of the cross-validation split
plain_explanation: Here the training data are cut into 5 folds (parts).

meaning: splitting method
plain_explanation: Every part has the same mix of fault classes, and near-identical records stay together in one part.

meaning: starting number for the random shuffle
plain_explanation: Recording it means the same split can be made again exactly (seed 20261010).

meaning: rank-based test for differences between groups
plain_explanation: Tests whether a gas differs between the fault classes without assuming a normal distribution.

meaning: Kruskal-Wallis test statistic
plain_explanation: The larger H is, the more the classes differ.

meaning: probability value
plain_explanation: The chance of seeing differences at least this large if there were really no difference; very small means a real difference.

meaning: effect size of the Kruskal-Wallis test
plain_explanation: How big the difference is, from 0 (none) to 1 (complete separation).

meaning: number of classes minus one here
plain_explanation: Needed to judge the H statistic (7 classes give 6).

meaning: middle value and the values a quarter and three quarters of the way up
plain_explanation: Describe typical gas levels without being pulled by extreme values.

meaning: rank correlation
plain_explanation: How strongly two gases rise and fall together (from -1 to +1).

meaning: logarithmic axis
plain_explanation: Each step on the axis is ten times the previous one, so very small and very large values fit on one chart.

meaning: comma-separated values
plain_explanation: A plain-text table file that any program can read.

meaning: image file, printable document file, dots per inch
plain_explanation: Figures are saved as PNG at 300 dpi (sharp for printing) and as PDF.

meaning: Microsoft Word document
plain_explanation: The format of these reports.

meaning: programming language
plain_explanation: Used for data preparation, machine learning and statistics (Claude Code).

meaning: virtual environment
plain_explanation: A private copy of Python and its libraries that belongs to this project only.

meaning: Windows Package Manager
plain_explanation: Windows tool used to install Python safely.

meaning: Python testing tool
plain_explanation: Runs the automated checks that prove the data rules hold.

meaning: YAML Ain't Markup Language
plain_explanation: A simple text format for settings files.

meaning: MATLAB (MathWorks)
plain_explanation: Numerical programming environment; used for the conventional methods and the dashboard (MATLAB Agentic Toolkit).

meaning: MATLAB's block-diagram modelling tool and its physical-modelling library
plain_explanation: Used to model the transformer's operating conditions (Simulink Agentic Toolkit); it never makes gas values.

meaning: numbered project decisions
plain_explanation: Decisions recorded in 00_Project_Admin/decisions_log.md; not the same as the fault codes D1 and D2.

meaning: the 45-step project plan
plain_explanation: Project_Roadmap.docx: every step, its environment and its outputs, done strictly in order.

meaning: Expected Results and Analysis Plan
plain_explanation: The approved document that fixes the measures, tests, tables and figures before results are seen.

meaning: the original document and a document that quotes it
plain_explanation: Values from a secondary source are marked TO VERIFY until checked against the primary source.

meaning: not yet checked against the original source
plain_explanation: Marks any value or fact that must still be confirmed before final use.

meaning: Rogers gas ratios
plain_explanation: R1 = CH4/H2, R2 = C2H2/C2H4, R5 = C2H4/C2H6; the three ratios the Rogers method compares with its table.

meaning: IEEE normal-level gas limits
plain_explanation: The highest gas levels at which IEEE C57.104 considers a transformer to be operating satisfactorily (e.g. H2 100 ppm, C2H2 1 ppm).

meaning: total dissolved combustible gas
plain_explanation: The sum of the combustible gases dissolved in the oil (all except CO2, O2 and N2).

meaning: older gas-ratio method by E. Doernenburg
plain_explanation: A four-ratio method in IEEE C57.104; not used in this thesis.

meaning: No diagnosis
plain_explanation: The answer of a method when no rule applies or a ratio it needs cannot be calculated. It is a result and is never deleted.

meaning: Two classes returned together
plain_explanation: Sometimes the IEC table fits two fault types at once. The method then answers with both (D1/D2); it counts as correct if the true class is either one.

meaning: Distance to the nearest decision boundary
plain_explanation: How far a sample is from the line where the diagnosis would change. A small distance means a small measurement error could change the diagnosis.

meaning: A factor of 10
plain_explanation: A distance of 1 decade on the ratio scale means the ratio is 10 times larger or smaller, e.g. from 0.1 to 1.

meaning: Rogers diagnosis code 0 to 5
plain_explanation: The Rogers table gives each combination of ratios a case number: 0 normal, 1 partial discharge, 2 arcing, 3 and 4 thermal below 700 degrees, 5 thermal above 700 degrees.

meaning: Result before and after the normality gate
plain_explanation: raw_result is what the method itself says; result is what is left after samples with low gas levels have been called Normal by the gate.

meaning: Cutting a shape with straight lines
plain_explanation: A standard way to find the area of the triangle that satisfies one limit after another; used to draw the Duval zones from their limits.

meaning: Automatic test of one small piece of code
plain_explanation: A test that feeds a function a known input and checks the answer, so that any later change that breaks the function is noticed at once.

meaning: Floating-point arithmetic standard
plain_explanation: The rule that decides how computers round decimal numbers; it makes a division that is exactly equal to a limit give exactly the limit.

meaning: chain of processing steps and a model
plain_explanation: Feature building, imputation, scaling and the classifier joined so that they are always fitted together on the same training rows.

meaning: the inputs given to a model
plain_explanation: F1 log gases, F2 gas percentages, F3 log-ratios and Duval percentages, F4 all of them (Analysis Plan 5.1).

meaning: logarithm of a gas ratio
plain_explanation: log10((a+1)/(b+1)); the +1 ppm keeps the value defined when a gas is not detected (decision D15).

meaning: filling in an undefined value
plain_explanation: An undefined Duval percentage is replaced by the median of the training fold (decision D15).

meaning: rescaling a feature
plain_explanation: Subtract the training-fold mean and divide by the training-fold standard deviation (Analysis Plan Eq. 13).

meaning: importance given to each record in training
plain_explanation: w_c = N/(K n_c): rare classes get more weight so that every class counts equally (Analysis Plan Eq. 14).

meaning: creating extra synthetic records of rare classes
plain_explanation: Not used in this thesis: it was never approved (decision D15).

meaning: cross-validation inside cross-validation
plain_explanation: The inner loop chooses the settings, the outer loop measures performance on data the tuning never saw.

meaning: list of settings tried for a model
plain_explanation: For example C and gamma of the SVM; the best combination is chosen in the inner loop (Analysis Plan 5.2).

meaning: average F1 score over the classes
plain_explanation: The primary performance measure; every class counts equally however rare it is.

meaning: turning SVM scores into probabilities
plain_explanation: A sigmoid curve fitted on internal cross-validation scores gives class probabilities (decision D16).

meaning: limited-memory BFGS optimiser
plain_explanation: The method that fits the neural network's weights; it converges reliably on small data sets (decision D16).

meaning: adaptive moment estimation optimiser
plain_explanation: The default neural-network optimiser in scikit-learn; it did not converge here and was replaced by L-BFGS.

meaning: standard deviation
plain_explanation: How much the 50 fold values spread around their mean; a small SD means the result is stable from fold to fold.

meaning: mean of the per-class recalls
plain_explanation: The share of each class that is found, averaged over the classes, so a rare class counts as much as a common one.

meaning: Cohen's kappa
plain_explanation: Agreement between predicted and true classes after removing the agreement expected by chance: 0 = chance, 1 = perfect.

meaning: Matthews correlation coefficient
plain_explanation: One score from -1 to 1 that uses the whole confusion matrix; 0 means no better than guessing.

meaning: harmonic mean of precision and recall
plain_explanation: High only when the model both finds the records of a class and is rarely wrong when it names that class.

meaning: test for two models compared on the same folds
plain_explanation: A t-test whose variance is enlarged because cross-validation folds share training records (Nadeau and Bengio, 2003; Analysis Plan Eq. 28).

meaning: rank-based comparison of several models
plain_explanation: Friedman tests whether models' average ranks over the folds differ; Nemenyi then shows which pairs differ (Step 30).

meaning: reference model
plain_explanation: Always predicts the most common class; any useful model must do clearly better.

meaning: mean position among the compared models
plain_explanation: In every fold the models are ranked by macro-F1 (1 = best); the ranks are then averaged over the folds.

meaning: training stopped at its step limit
plain_explanation: The training algorithm used all allowed iterations before reaching its stopping tolerance; the result may be slightly less than optimal.

meaning: radial basis function
plain_explanation: The kernel that lets the SVM draw curved boundaries between classes.

meaning: table of true against predicted classes
plain_explanation: Each row is a true class, each column a predicted class; the diagonal holds the correct answers, every other cell a particular mistake.

meaning: test data differ from training data
plain_explanation: Records from another laboratory, country or labelling practice can follow a different pattern, so a model usually scores lower on them than in cross-validation.

meaning: model's confidence in each class
plain_explanation: For every record the model gives a probability for each of the seven classes; they add up to 1 and the largest is the prediction.

meaning: Python file format for saved models
plain_explanation: Stores the fitted pipeline (preprocessing and model together) so it can be reloaded and give exactly the same predictions.

meaning: drop in score when one input is shuffled
plain_explanation: The values of one input are mixed up at random across records; the bigger the drop in macro-F1, the more the model relies on that input (Analysis Plan Eq. 38).

meaning: shuffling one gas and everything made from it
plain_explanation: One raw gas is shuffled before the features are built, so all its ratios and percentages move together; this avoids under-rating gases whose information is shared by several features.

meaning: exact SHAP calculation for tree models
plain_explanation: An algorithm that computes SHAP values of a tree ensemble exactly and quickly, without approximation.

meaning: one dot per record and feature
plain_explanation: Each dot shows how much one feature pushed one record towards a class; its colour shows whether the feature value was high or low.

meaning: the gas most typical of a fault type
plain_explanation: For example hydrogen for partial discharge, acetylene for arcing and ethylene for severe overheating; used to judge whether the model reasons like an engineer.

meaning: short fact sheet of a model
plain_explanation: States what the model is for and not for, its inputs, training data, measured performance and limitations (Mitchell et al., 2019).

meaning: testing the model with fewer gases
plain_explanation: The model is retrained with only some gases available, to see how much accuracy is lost - relevant for monitors that measure fewer gases.

meaning: instrument fitted to a transformer
plain_explanation: Measures dissolved gases continuously in service; many measure only some of the five gases.

meaning: Not a Number, used here for a gas that was not measured
plain_explanation: A marker for a missing value. It is different from 0 ppm: 0 ppm means the gas was measured and not found, NaN means nobody measured it, so no ratio or percentage can be calculated from it.

meaning: A method that has all the gases it needs
plain_explanation: A method is applicable to a gas combination when every gas it uses is measured. IEC 60599 and Rogers need all five gases; Duval Triangle 1 needs CH4, C2H4 and C2H2. If a method is not applicable it answers ND for every sample.

meaning: A choice of the gases that are measured
plain_explanation: One of the 31 ways to keep at least one of the five gases, as with an online monitor that measures only some gases.

meaning: resampling to get a confidence interval
plain_explanation: The records are drawn again at random, with replacement and within each fault class, 2000 times; the middle 95 % of the recomputed values is the 95 % interval (Analysis Plan Section 6.2).

meaning: fewest gases that are good enough
plain_explanation: The smallest gas combination whose loss of macro-F1, at the upper end of its 95 % interval, stays within the approved tolerance of 0.05 (Analysis Plan Eq. 37).

meaning: largest acceptable loss
plain_explanation: Fixed before the study at 0.05 macro-F1 (5 percentage points), approved in Step 4.

meaning: correct answers out of all records
plain_explanation: Every no-diagnosis (ND) counts as wrong, because the engineer got no help (Analysis Plan Eq. 7).

meaning: correct answers out of the records answered
plain_explanation: Looks only at the cases where the method gave a diagnosis (Analysis Plan Eq. 7).

meaning: share of records that get a diagnosis
plain_explanation: 1 minus the share of no-diagnosis answers (Analysis Plan Eq. 6); the ML model always answers, so its coverage is 100 %.

meaning: confidence interval for a proportion
plain_explanation: A 95 % interval for an accuracy or a coverage that works well for small samples (Analysis Plan Eq. 21).

meaning: benchmark used when the method was built
plain_explanation: The IEC 60599 limits were refined with the IEC TC 10 cases, so the conventional methods may score higher on that benchmark than on new data.

meaning: paired test of two methods on the same records
plain_explanation: Uses only the records where one method is right and the other wrong (b and c); tests whether b and c differ more than chance (Analysis Plan Eqs. 30-31).

meaning: test of several methods on the same records
plain_explanation: Tests whether all methods have the same share of correct answers before the pairwise tests (Analysis Plan Eq. 29).

meaning: adjustment for several tests
plain_explanation: Keeps the chance of any false positive among the three comparisons per test set at 5 % (Analysis Plan Eq. 32).

meaning: smallest significant gap in average rank
plain_explanation: Two models whose average ranks differ by less than the CD cannot be told apart (Nemenyi test, Analysis Plan Eq. 27).

meaning: effect size of the McNemar test
plain_explanation: How many times more often the ML model was right where the other method was wrong than the reverse; 1 = no difference.

meaning: model for a yes/no outcome
plain_explanation: Estimates how the chance that ML and a conventional method disagree changes with the distance to the nearest decision boundary (Analysis Plan Eq. 33).

meaning: how far a sample lies from a decision line
plain_explanation: For the ratio methods in decades of the ratio, for Duval in percentage points to the nearest zone edge (Analysis Plan Eqs. 9-10).

meaning: exploratory improvement study
plain_explanation: An extra study, planned after the main results, that tests ways to improve the model; reported separately from the main (confirmatory) results.

meaning: tested as planned vs looked into afterwards
plain_explanation: Confirmatory results test a hypothesis fixed in advance on untouched data; exploratory results come from analyses planned after seeing some results and need confirmation on new data.

meaning: writing the plan before the analysis
plain_explanation: The questions, data rules, methods and decision rules are fixed and fingerprinted before any result exists, so the analysis cannot be fitted to the results.

meaning: testing on a source never seen in training
plain_explanation: Each data source is held out in turn; the model is trained on the other sources and tested on the held-out one, which measures how well it transfers to new data.

meaning: machine learning plus expert rules
plain_explanation: A model that receives the conventional methods' answers and boundary distances as extra inputs besides the gas features.

meaning: the model may decline to answer
plain_explanation: The model gives a diagnosis only when its highest class probability reaches a threshold; otherwise it reports no diagnosis (Chow, 1970).

meaning: accuracy on the records the model chose to answer
plain_explanation: With a reject option, the share of correct answers among the records whose top probability reached the threshold.

meaning: comparing at the same answer rate
plain_explanation: The model's threshold is set so it answers exactly as many records as a conventional method does; then both accuracies are compared.

meaning: MathWorks block-diagram simulation environment
plain_explanation: Software in which the model is drawn as blocks and lines and simulated over time.

meaning: Physical modelling extension of Simulink
plain_explanation: Blocks that follow physical laws (electrical, thermal) and connect like real components, not like signals.

meaning: A group of blocks shown as one block
plain_explanation: The model is split into seven subsystems: grid, transformer, measurement, load, losses to heat, thermal network, outputs and ageing.

meaning: Block that sets the numerical solver of a physical network
plain_explanation: Every physical network (the electrical one and the thermal one) needs exactly one of these blocks.

meaning: Text note placed on a model diagram
plain_explanation: A short description of what a subsystem does, its inputs, outputs and parameters, written on the diagram so that a reader does not need the code.

meaning: Temperature of the oil at the top of the tank
plain_explanation: The oil temperature used in the thermal model; it rises with load and falls back towards ambient.

meaning: Temperature of the hottest part of the winding
plain_explanation: The winding temperature that mostly decides how fast the paper insulation ages; it is the top-oil temperature plus a load-dependent rise.

meaning: Load current divided by rated current
plain_explanation: K = 1 means the transformer carries its rated current; K = 0.5 means half of it.

meaning: How many times faster than normal the paper ages
plain_explanation: V = 1 at the reference hot-spot temperature (98 degC); every 6 K more doubles it. The loss of life is the sum of V over time.

meaning: Value divided by its rated value
plain_explanation: A way of writing quantities so that 1.0 means rated, e.g. a current of 1.0 pu is the rated current.

meaning: IEC loading guide for oil-immersed power transformers
plain_explanation: The standard that gives the equations for oil and hot-spot temperature and for ageing under a changing load.

meaning: Fast solver setting for power networks
plain_explanation: Lets a 50 Hz network be simulated with large time steps; it accepts only linear equations, which is why the arithmetic is done outside the physical network.

meaning: MathWorks tool that checks a Simulink model against a list of rules
plain_explanation: A built-in inspector. It runs many checks (settings, unconnected ports, style rules) and reports each as passed, warning or failed.

meaning: MathWorks Advisory Board (modelling style guidelines)
plain_explanation: A set of style rules for control-system models. Some of them do not suit a physical plant model and are accepted with a reason.

meaning: Simulink command that compiles the model without running it
plain_explanation: Finds errors such as unconnected ports or wrong units before the simulation is run (Ctrl+D).

meaning: Reactance seen by currents that are equal in all three phases
plain_explanation: Matters only for unbalanced faults to earth; it has no effect when the three phases are loaded equally, as in this model.

meaning: MathWorks tool that stores and compares logged simulation signals
plain_explanation: A viewer in which the signals of each run are kept, so runs can be compared or saved as a session file.

meaning: Largest absolute difference between model and reference over the compared time points
plain_explanation: The worst-case error of the model, in kelvin. It must stay within 0.1 K.

meaning: Square root of the mean of the squared differences
plain_explanation: A typical size of the error over the whole run, less sensitive to a single worst point than the largest difference.

meaning: Exact formula for the answer, with no numerical solver
plain_explanation: For a constant load the oil and winding temperatures follow simple exponential curves; this formula is an independent check of the model and of the numerical reference.

meaning: Time for a first-order quantity to reach 63.2 % (1 - 1/e) of its final change
plain_explanation: For the top-oil temperature this time equals the oil time constant times k11, i.e. 75 minutes here.

meaning: Equivalent hours of insulation ageing at the reference hot-spot temperature
plain_explanation: The sum of the ageing rate over time: L = 24 h would mean the insulation aged as much as in 24 hours at 98 degC.

meaning: Load above rated current
plain_explanation: A load factor above 1.0 per unit; the hot spot heats quickly and the ageing rate rises steeply.

meaning: A chosen load history used to run the model
plain_explanation: An illustrative example of how the transformer is loaded over time (constant, daily cycle, overload); it is not measured data.

meaning: A moment in simulated time at which a gas sample would be taken
plain_explanation: The model only says when; the gas values come from the real measured record in the data file, never from the model.

meaning: A record of the master table that is not used for development
plain_explanation: A record kept aside (benchmark, internal test or external test) so that the methods are judged on data they did not learn from.

meaning: Relative accuracy that the variable-step solver keeps at each step
plain_explanation: A smaller RelTol makes the solver take smaller steps: the result is more exact and the run slower.

meaning: Lamp that says whether the conventional methods agree with the ML diagnosis
plain_explanation: Green: all three conventional methods give the same class as ML. Amber: at least one does not. Grey: no ML answer.

meaning: MATLAB function that sends data to a web service
plain_explanation: How the dashboard sends the five gas values to the FastAPI service and receives the ML class.

meaning: MATLAB tool for building apps (.mlapp files)
plain_explanation: The program in which DGADashboard.mlapp is edited; the file can also be run without opening it.

meaning: List of the sampling events of a simulated run in the dashboard
plain_explanation: One row per sampling event: time, record, ML class, how many conventional methods agree, and the simulated hot-spot temperature at that time.

meaning: Showing the sampling events of a finished run one after the other
plain_explanation: The dashboard steps through the events in time order and diagnoses the record of each.

meaning: One of the first calls to the service, which can be slower than the later ones
plain_explanation: The first few requests set up the connection; they are flagged in the log so that they can be excluded or kept openly.

meaning: Time between sending a request to the service and receiving the answer
plain_explanation: How long the engineer waits for the ML diagnosis; reported as the median and the 95th percentile.

meaning: application programming interface
plain_explanation: A fixed way for one program to ask another for something; here the dashboard asks the Python service for a diagnosis.

meaning: Hypertext Transfer Protocol
plain_explanation: The message format of the web; the dashboard sends a request and the service sends back an answer with a status code (200 = OK, 422 = input refused).

meaning: JavaScript Object Notation
plain_explanation: A plain-text format for named values, e.g. {"H2": 200}; requests and answers of the service are written in it.

meaning: standard description of a web interface
plain_explanation: A file that lists every address of the service, what it must be sent and what it answers, so another program can be built against it.

meaning: Python framework for web services
plain_explanation: The library used to build the diagnosis service; it also checks every input against the declared rules.

meaning: one address of a web service
plain_explanation: For example POST /diagnose (send a sample, get a diagnosis) or GET /health (is the service alive?).

meaning: the address of the computer itself
plain_explanation: A service on 127.0.0.1 can be reached only from the same computer, not from the network.

meaning: the value below which 95 % of the measurements lie
plain_explanation: Used for the response time: 95 of every 100 requests are answered at least this fast.

meaning: share of records for which the service gives exactly the offline answer
plain_explanation: F = matches / records sent (Analysis Plan Eq. 47); the requirement is 100 %.

meaning: share of measurements at or below each value

meaning: the integrated system run over every held-out record
